summary: Implemented the ADR-024 F7 discriminator and the owned empty-selection restore/removal behavior (Phase 20 task 20.1). (1) RenderPassThroughReason.NoDisplayableValue is narrowed to exactly an empty resolved BadgeSelection and a distinct bounded NoFittingBadge reason is added for a non-empty selection whose layout is empty; SkiaBadgeRenderer emits NoDisplayableValue for the selection.IsEmpty branch and NoFittingBadge for the layout.IsEmpty branch. (2) ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.GenerateCoreAsync now routes a NoDisplayableValue render pass-through on an item/surface with a live owned Published session to the existing guarded restoration path (the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync entry point) instead of returning early; the publisher restores the retained baseline or removes the ArrTags image when the baseline was absent, records the durable Restoration ArtworkOperation before mutation, and resumes it through the existing restart recovery gate. (3) The coordinator reads the optional durable ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore (absent store means Normal, mirroring ArtworkPublisher) and refuses to call RestoreAsync when ArtworkLifecycleFenceState.AllowsNewRestoration is false, so an ItemRemoved or invalid fence performs no mutation. (4) The result records the bounded restore/removal classification: a new ArtworkGenerationOutcome.Restored plus the bounded ArtworkReconciliationOutcome on ArtworkGenerationResult (Completed = the retained baseline was restored, or the ArrTags image removed when the baseline was absent; otherwise the bounded refusal/uncertainty classification), with no RenderVersion, renderer-configuration schema, or fingerprint change. (5) Every other pass-through reason (NoMetadata, NoFittingBadge, IneligibleSurface, MatchNotEligible, SourceUnavailable) preserves the owned artwork with no mutation and a non-owned item stays a plain pass-through. interpretations.question: Which ArtworkGenerationOutcome value should record a restoration that did not complete (a fence refusal, an ownership change, an uncertain readback, or a cancellation)?
interpretations.chosen: Only a Completed reconciliation produces the new Restored outcome. A cancellation produces Cancelled; NothingToReconcile (the guarded path was refused or the state changed before it ran) keeps RenderPassThrough; every other reconciliation outcome produces Blocked. Every driven restoration carries the bounded ArtworkReconciliationOutcome, so the specific classification is never lost.
interpretations.basis: ADR-024 clause 7 asks for a bounded generation result that records the restore/removal classification (the task names 'a new ArtworkGenerationOutcome value plus the bounded ArtworkReconciliationOutcome'). Completed is the only reconciliation outcome that changed the active artwork, so mapping refused/uncertain results to Restored would contradict the truthful reading of the outcome name and the Preserved invariant.
interpretations.impact: Result classification only. The outcome (including Restored) appears in the bounded artwork-boundary log line through the existing result.Outcome and the bounded reason text; the specific ReconciliationOutcome stays on the result and is not emitted in the log (see the log-scope interpretation below). Nothing is persisted and no fingerprint or render output changes.

interpretations.question: Should the coordinator call ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync when the current durable fence refuses restoration (for example a confirmed item removal), or let the publisher refuse it?
interpretations.chosen: The coordinator refuses locally: it returns a plain preserved pass-through with no RestoreAsync call, no reconciliation outcome, and no mutation. The publisher's own refusal remains the second layer.
interpretations.basis: ADR-024 clause 2 (drive the restore under the current durable fence, which AllowsNewRestoration permits during normal operation) and the task's 'a non-restorable fence must not cause a mutation'. A local refusal makes the guarantee observable and avoids a pointless call; the publisher still refuses even if a caller bypassed the coordinator check (probe P5 showed the publisher refused the ItemRemoved fence).
interpretations.impact: A refused restore reports ReconciliationOutcome null rather than NothingToReconcile. Under a Disable/Uninstall fence restoration stays permitted and the existing lifecycle drain owns the bulk restoration; under ItemRemoved or an invalid fence the coordinator makes no restore call. No image mutation in either case.

interpretations.question: How is a completed absent-baseline removal distinguished from a completed baseline restoration in the bounded result?
interpretations.chosen: Both produce Restored + ArtworkReconciliationOutcome.Completed; the committed state carried on the result (State.SourcePresence = Absent for a removal, Present for a restoration) distinguishes them, matching the publisher's existing Completed result and Restored state transitions.
interpretations.basis: ArtworkReconciliationOutcome has a single Completed value for both cases and the committed PublishedArtworkState already carries SourcePresence; inventing a second outcome value for removal would duplicate state the publisher already commits.
interpretations.impact: The bounded classification stays inside the existing enums; a consumer that needs restore-vs-removal reads the committed state. The absent-baseline removal is not reachable through the coordinator (ReadRetainedSource returns Absent -> NoSource before rendering) and is exercised by the task 20.2 direct publisher test.

interpretations.question: Should the artwork log line be extended to emit the new bounded ArtworkReconciliationOutcome as a classification qualifier (like the F8 PassThroughReason/FailureReason qualifiers)?
interpretations.chosen: No. The result records the classification; the existing log line already emits the outcome (including Restored) and the NoDisplayableValue pass-through reason, and no log format change was made.
interpretations.basis: ADR-024 clause 7 requires the generation result to record the classification and explicitly makes no render output change; task 15.3's F8 log contract enumerates the render/source/failure enums and does not name the reconciliation outcome.
interpretations.impact: The bounded reconciliation outcome is consumed by callers/tests rather than the artwork log; the log still distinguishes Restored from RenderPassThrough/Blocked and carries the reason text. Extending the log would be a task 20.2/20.3 decision.
